1.sahih_international: O you who covers himself [with a garment],
1.pickthall: O thou enveloped in thy cloak,
1.yusuf_ali: O thou wrapped up (in the mantle)!
1.arberry: O thou shrouded in thy mantle,

3.yusuf_ali: And thy Lord do thou magnify!
3.muhammad_sarwar: proclaim the greatness of your Lord,

4.yusuf_ali: And thy garments keep free from stain!

5.mohsin_khan: And keep away from Ar-Rujz (the idols)!

6.sahih_international: And do not confer favor to acquire more
6.pickthall: And show not favour, seeking wordly gain!
6.yusuf_ali: Nor expect, in giving, any increase (for thyself)!
6.shakir: And bestow not favors that you may receive again with increase,
6.muhammad_sarwar: and do not think that by doing such deeds, you have done a great favor to God.
6.mohsin_khan: And give not a thing in order to have more (or consider not your deeds of Allah's obedience as a favour to Allah).
6.arberry: Give not, thinking to gain greater

7.sahih_international: But for your Lord be patient.
7.pickthall: For the sake of thy Lord, be patient!
7.yusuf_ali: But, for thy Lord's (Cause), be patient and constant!
7.shakir: And for the sake of your Lord, be patient.
7.muhammad_sarwar: Exercise patience to please your Lord.
7.mohsin_khan: And be patient for the sake of your Lord (i.e. perform your duty to Allah)!
7.arberry: and be patient unto thy Lord.

8.sahih_international: And when the trumpet is blown,
8.pickthall: For when the trumpet shall sound,
8.yusuf_ali: Finally, when the Trumpet is sounded,
8.shakir: For when the trumpet is sounded,
8.mohsin_khan: Then, when the Trumpet is sounded (i.e. its second blowing);
8.arberry: For when the Trump is sounded

9.sahih_international: That Day will be a difficult day
9.pickthall: Surely that day will be a day of anguish,
9.yusuf_ali: That will be- that Day - a Day of Distress,-
9.shakir: That, at that time, shall be a difficult day,
9.muhammad_sarwar: it will be a hard day
9.mohsin_khan: Truly, that Day will be a Hard Day.
9.arberry: that day will be a harsh day,

10.yusuf_ali: Far from easy for those without Faith.
10.shakir: For the unbelievers, anything but easy.
10.muhammad_sarwar: and for the disbelievers, in particular, it will not be at all easy.
10.mohsin_khan: Far from easy for the disbelievers.

11.sahih_international: Leave Me with the one I created alone
11.pickthall: Leave Me (to deal) with him whom I created lonely,
11.yusuf_ali: Leave Me alone, (to deal) with the (creature) whom I created (bare and) alone!-
11.shakir: Leave Me and him whom I created alone,
11.muhammad_sarwar: Leave to Me the one, whom I have created all by Myself,
11.mohsin_khan: Leave Me Alone (to deal) with whom I created Alone (without any means, i.e. Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi)!
11.arberry: Leave Me with him whom I created alone,

12.sahih_international: And to whom I granted extensive wealth
12.pickthall: And then bestowed upon him ample means,
12.yusuf_ali: To whom I granted resources in abundance,
12.muhammad_sarwar: and whom I have granted abundant wealth
12.mohsin_khan: And then granted him resources in abundance.
12.arberry: and appointed for him ample wealth

13.pickthall: And sons abiding in his presence
13.yusuf_ali: And sons to be by his side!-
13.shakir: And sons dwelling in his presence,
13.muhammad_sarwar: and children living in his presence,
13.mohsin_khan: And children to be by his side!

14.sahih_international: And spread [everything] before him, easing [his life].
14.yusuf_ali: To whom I made (life) smooth and comfortable!
14.shakir: And I adjusted affairs for him adjustably;
14.muhammad_sarwar: whose life I have made run smoothly
14.mohsin_khan: And made life smooth and comfortable for him!
14.arberry: and made all things smooth for him;

15.sahih_international: Then he desires that I should add more.
15.pickthall: Yet he desireth that I should give more.
15.yusuf_ali: Yet is he greedy-that I should add (yet more);-
15.shakir: And yet he desires that I should add more!
15.mohsin_khan: After all that he desires that I should give more;
15.arberry: then he is eager that I should do more.

16.sahih_international: No! Indeed, he has been toward Our verses obstinate.
16.pickthall: Nay! For lo! he hath been stubborn to Our revelations.
16.yusuf_ali: By no means! For to Our Signs he has been refractory!
16.shakir: By no means! surely he offers opposition to Our communications.
16.muhammad_sarwar: Never will he receive more. He has been hostile to Our revelations.
16.mohsin_khan: Nay! Verily, he has been stubborn and opposing Our Ayat (proofs, evidences, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.).
16.arberry: Nay! He is forward unto Our signs;

17.sahih_international: I will cover him with arduous torment.
17.pickthall: On him I shall impose a fearful doom.
17.yusuf_ali: Soon will I visit him with a mount of calamities!
17.shakir: I will make a distressing punishment overtake him.
17.muhammad_sarwar: We shall make him suffer the torment of hell without relief.
17.mohsin_khan: I shall oblige him to (climb a slippery mountain in the Hell-fire called As-Sa'ud, or to) face a severe torment!
17.arberry: and I shall constrain him to a hard ascent.

18.pickthall: For lo! he did consider; then he planned -
18.yusuf_ali: For he thought and he plotted;-

19.sahih_international: So may he be destroyed [for] how he deliberated.
19.yusuf_ali: And woe to him! How he plotted!-
19.shakir: But may he be cursed how he plotted;
19.mohsin_khan: So let him be cursed! How he plotted!
19.arberry: death seize him, how he determined!

20.sahih_international: Then may he be destroyed [for] how he deliberated.
20.pickthall: Again (self-)destroyed is he, how he planned! -
20.yusuf_ali: Yea, Woe to him; How he plotted!-
20.shakir: Again, may he be cursed how he plotted;
20.muhammad_sarwar: What an evil plan he has made!
20.mohsin_khan: And once more let him be cursed, how he plotted!
20.arberry: Again, death seize him, how he determined!

21.muhammad_sarwar: May he be condemned again for his schemes! He looked around,

22.pickthall: Then frowned he and showed displeasure.
22.yusuf_ali: Then he frowned and he scowled;
22.mohsin_khan: Then he frowned and he looked in a bad tempered way;

23.sahih_international: Then he turned back and was arrogant
23.pickthall: Then turned he away in pride
23.yusuf_ali: Then he turned back and was haughty;
23.shakir: Then he turned back and was big with pride,
23.muhammad_sarwar: then turned back, and swelling-up with pride,
23.mohsin_khan: Then he turned back and was proud;
23.arberry: then he retreated, and waxed proud.

24.sahih_international: And said, "This is not but magic imitated [from others].
24.pickthall: And said: This is naught else than magic from of old;
24.yusuf_ali: Then said he: "This is nothing but magic, derived from of old;
24.shakir: ~Then he said: This is naught but enchantment, narrated (from others);
24.muhammad_sarwar: said, "This (the Quran) is nothing but magic, inherited from ancient magicians.
24.mohsin_khan: Then he said: "This is nothing but magic from that of old;
24.arberry: He said, 'This is naught but a trumped-up sorcery;

25.sahih_international: This is not but the word of a human being."
25.pickthall: This is naught else than speech of mortal man.
25.yusuf_ali: "This is nothing but the word of a mortal!"
25.shakir: This is naught but the word of a mortal.
25.muhammad_sarwar: These are only words from a mere mortal".
25.mohsin_khan: "This is nothing but the word of a human being!"

26.sahih_international: I will drive him into Saqar.
26.pickthall: Him shall I fling unto the burning.
26.yusuf_ali: Soon will I cast him into Hell-Fire!
26.shakir: I will cast him into hell.
26.muhammad_sarwar: I shall make him suffer the torment of hell.
26.mohsin_khan: I will cast him into Hell-fire
26.arberry: I shall surely roast him in Sakar;

27.sahih_international: And what can make you know what is Saqar?
27.pickthall: - Ah, what will convey unto thee what that burning is! -
27.yusuf_ali: And what will explain to thee what Hell-Fire is?
27.shakir: And what will make you realize what hell is?
27.muhammad_sarwar: Would that you really knew what hell is!
27.mohsin_khan: And what will make you know exactly what Hell-fire is?
27.arberry: and what will teach thee what is Sakar?

28.sahih_international: It lets nothing remain and leaves nothing [unburned],
28.pickthall: It leaveth naught; it spareth naught
28.yusuf_ali: Naught doth it permit to endure, and naught doth it leave alone!-
28.shakir: It leaves naught nor does it spare aught.
28.muhammad_sarwar: It leaves and spares no one and nothing.
28.mohsin_khan: It spares not (any sinner), nor does it leave (anything unburnt)!
28.arberry: It spares not, neither leaves alone

29.yusuf_ali: Darkening and changing the colour of man!

30.muhammad_sarwar: and it has nineteen angelic keepers.
30.mohsin_khan: Over it are nineteen (angels as guardians and keepers of Hell).

31.sahih_international: And We have not made the keepers of the Fire except angels. And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve - that those who were given the Scripture will be convinced and those who have believed will increase in faith and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt and that those in whose hearts is hypocrisy and the disbelievers will say, "What does Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus does Allah leave astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And mention of the Fire is not but a reminder to humanity.
31.pickthall: We have appointed only angels to be wardens of the Fire, and their number have We made to be a stumbling-block for those who disbelieve; that those to whom the Scripture hath been given may have certainty, and that believers may increase in faith; and that those to whom the Scripture hath been given and believers may not doubt; and that those in whose hearts there is disease, and disbelievers, may say: What meaneth Allah by this similitude? Thus Allah sendeth astray whom He will, and whom He will He guideth. None knoweth the hosts of thy Lord save Him. This is naught else than a Reminder unto mortals.
31.yusuf_ali: And We have set none but angels as Guardians of the Fire; and We have fixed their number only as a trial for Unbelievers,- in order that the People of the Book may arrive at certainty, and the Believers may increase in Faith,- and that no doubts may be left for the People of the Book and the Believers, and that those in whose hearts is a disease and the Unbelievers may say, "What symbol doth Allah intend by this?" Thus doth Allah leave to stray whom He pleaseth, and guide whom He pleaseth: and none can know the forces of thy Lord, except He and this is no other than a warning to mankind.
31.shakir: And We have not made the wardens of the fire others than angels, and We have not made their number but as a trial for those who disbelieve, that those who have been given the book may be certain and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who have been given the book and the believers may not doubt, and that those in whose hearts is a disease and the unbelievers may say: What does Allah mean by this parable? Thus does Allah make err whom He pleases, and He guides whom He pleases, and none knows the hosts of your Lord but He Himself; and this is naught but a reminder to the mortals.
31.muhammad_sarwar: We have made only angels as the keepers of the fire (for they are the strongest in carrying out Our commands). Our informing (people) of the numbers of these angels is a trial for the disbelievers. It gives more certainty to the people of the Book and strengthens the faith of the believers. The people of the Book and the believers have no doubt about it. We have fixed the number to make the disbelievers and those whose hearts are sick say, "What does God mean by such a parable?" Thus, God guides and causes to go astray whomever He wants. No one knows about the army of your Lord except He Himself. This parable is a reminder for mankind.
31.mohsin_khan: And We have set none but angels as guardians of the Fire, and We have fixed their number (19) only as a trial for the disbelievers, in order that the people of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) may arrive at a certainty [that this Quran is the truth as it agrees with their Books i.e. their number (19) is written in the Taurat (Torah) and the Injeel (Gospel)] and the believers may increase in Faith (as this Quran is the truth) and that no doubts may be left for the people of the Scripture and the believers, and that those in whose hearts is a disease (of hypocrisy) and the disbelievers may say: "What Allah intends by this (curious) example?" Thus Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And none can know the hosts of your Lord but He. And this (Hell) is nothing else than a (warning) reminder to mankind.
31.arberry: We have appointed only angels to be masters of the Fire, and their number We have appointed only as a trial for the unbelievers, that those who were given the Book may have certainty, and that those who believe may increase in belief, and that those who were given the Book and those who believe may not be in-doubt, and that those in whose hearts there is sickness, and the unbelievers, may say, 'What did God intend by this as a similitude?' So God leads astray whomsoever He will, and He guides whomsoever He will; and none knows the hosts of thy Lord but He. And it is naught but a Reminder to mortals.

32.shakir: Nay; I swear by the moon,

33.sahih_international: And [by] the night when it departs
33.pickthall: And the night when it withdraweth
33.yusuf_ali: And by the Night as it retreateth,
33.shakir: And the night when it departs,
33.mohsin_khan: And by the night when it withdraws,
33.arberry: and the night when it retreats

34.sahih_international: And [by] the morning when it brightens,
34.pickthall: And the dawn when it shineth forth,
34.yusuf_ali: And by the Dawn as it shineth forth,-
34.shakir: And the daybreak when it shines;
34.mohsin_khan: And by the dawn when it brightens,
34.arberry: and the dawn when it is white,

35.sahih_international: Indeed, the Fire is of the greatest [afflictions]
35.pickthall: Lo! this is one of the greatest (portents)
35.yusuf_ali: This is but one of the mighty (portents),
35.shakir: Surely it (hell) is one of the gravest (misfortunes),
35.muhammad_sarwar: hell is certainly the greatest calamity.
35.mohsin_khan: Verily, it (Hell, or their denial of the Prophet Muhammad SAW, or the Day of Resurrection) is but one of the greatest calamities.
35.arberry: surely it is one of the greatest things

36.muhammad_sarwar: It is a warning for mankind

37.sahih_international: To whoever wills among you to proceed or stay behind.
37.pickthall: Unto him of you who will advance or hang back.
37.yusuf_ali: To any of you that chooses to press forward, or to follow behind;-
37.shakir: To him among you who wishes to go forward or remain behind.
37.muhammad_sarwar: whether one steps forward to embrace the faith or one turns away from it.
37.mohsin_khan: To any of you that chooses to go forward (by working righteous deeds), or to remain behind (by commiting sins),
37.arberry: to whoever of you desires to go forward or lag behind.

38.sahih_international: Every soul, for what it has earned, will be retained
38.pickthall: Every soul is a pledge for its own deeds;
38.yusuf_ali: Every soul will be (held) in pledge for its deeds.
38.shakir: Every soul is held in pledge for what it earns,
38.muhammad_sarwar: Every soul will be in captivity for its deeds
38.mohsin_khan: Every person is a pledge for what he has earned,
38.arberry: Every soul shall be pledged for what it has earned,

39.sahih_international: Except the companions of the right,
39.pickthall: Save those who will stand on the right hand.
39.yusuf_ali: Except the Companions of the Right Hand.
39.shakir: Except the people of the right hand,
39.muhammad_sarwar: except the people of the right hand
39.mohsin_khan: Except those on the Right, (i.e. the pious true believers of Islamic Monotheism);
39.arberry: save the Companions of the Right;

40.sahih_international: [Who will be] in gardens, questioning each other
40.pickthall: In gardens they will ask one another
40.yusuf_ali: (They will be) in Gardens (of Delight): they will question each other,
40.shakir: In gardens, they shall ask each other
40.mohsin_khan: In Gardens (Paradise) they will ask one another,

41.muhammad_sarwar: and will ask of the criminals,
41.mohsin_khan: About Al-Mujrimun (polytheists, criminals, disbelievers, etc.), (And they will say to them):

42.sahih_international: [And asking them], "What put you into Saqar?"
42.pickthall: What hath brought you to this burning?
42.shakir: What has brought you into hell?
42.mohsin_khan: "What has caused you to enter Hell?"

43.sahih_international: They will say, "We were not of those who prayed,
43.pickthall: They will answer: We were not of those who prayed
43.yusuf_ali: They will say: "We were not of those who prayed;
43.shakir: They shall say: We were not of those who prayed;
43.muhammad_sarwar: They will reply, "We did not pray,
43.mohsin_khan: They will say: "We were not of those who used to offer their Salat (prayers)
43.arberry: They shall say, 'We were not of those who prayed, and

44.sahih_international: Nor did we used to feed the poor.
44.pickthall: Nor did we feed the wretched.
44.yusuf_ali: "Nor were we of those who fed the indigent;
44.shakir: And we used not to feed the poor;
44.muhammad_sarwar: nor did we feed the destitute.
44.mohsin_khan: "Nor we used to feed Al-Miskin (the poor);

45.sahih_international: And we used to enter into vain discourse with those who engaged [in it],
45.pickthall: We used to wade (in vain dispute) with (all) waders,
45.yusuf_ali: "But we used to talk vanities with vain talkers;
45.shakir: And we used to enter into vain discourse with those who entered into vain discourses.
45.muhammad_sarwar: We indulged and persisted in useless disputes,
45.mohsin_khan: "And we used to talk falsehood (all that which Allah hated) with vain talkers.
45.arberry: and we plunged along with the plungers,

46.sahih_international: And we used to deny the Day of Recompense
46.pickthall: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment,
46.yusuf_ali: "And we used to deny the Day of Judgment,
46.shakir: And we used to call the day of judgment a lie;
46.muhammad_sarwar: and rejected the Day of Judgment
46.mohsin_khan: "And we used to belie the Day of Recompense
46.arberry: and we cried lies to the Day of Doom,

47.sahih_international: Until there came to us the certainty."
47.pickthall: Till the Inevitable came unto us.
47.yusuf_ali: "Until there came to us (the Hour) that is certain."
47.mohsin_khan: "Until there came to us (the death) that is certain."
47.arberry: till the Certain came to us.' --

48.sahih_international: So there will not benefit them the intercession of [any] intercessors.
48.pickthall: The mediation of no mediators will avail them then.
48.yusuf_ali: Then will no intercession of (any) intercessors profit them.
48.shakir: So the intercession of intercessors shall not avail them.
48.muhammad_sarwar: The intercession of the intercessors will be of no benefit to them.
48.mohsin_khan: So no intercession of intercessors will be of any use to them.
48.arberry: Then the intercession of the intercessors shall not profit them.

49.sahih_international: Then what is [the matter] with them that they are, from the reminder, turning away
49.pickthall: Why now turn they away from the Admonishment,
49.yusuf_ali: Then what is the matter with them that they turn away from admonition?-
49.shakir: What is then the matter with them, that they turn away from the admonition
49.muhammad_sarwar: If such will be the Day of Judgment, what is the matter with them? Why do they run away from guidance,
49.mohsin_khan: Then what is wrong with them (i.e. the disbelievers) that they turn away from (receiving) admonition?
49.arberry: What ails them, that they turn away from the Reminder,

50.sahih_international: As if they were alarmed donkeys
50.yusuf_ali: As if they were affrighted asses,
50.shakir: As if they were asses taking fright
50.mohsin_khan: As if they were frightened (wild) donkeys.
50.arberry: as if they were startled asses

51.shakir: That had fled from a lion?
51.mohsin_khan: Fleeing from a hunter, or a lion, or a beast of prey.

52.sahih_international: Rather, every person among them desires that he would be given scriptures spread about.
52.pickthall: Nay, but everyone of them desireth that he should be given open pages (from Allah).
52.yusuf_ali: Forsooth, each one of them wants to be given scrolls (of revelation) spread out!
52.shakir: Nay; every one of them desires that he may be given pages spread out;
52.muhammad_sarwar: Is it that everyone of them wants to receive a heavenly book addressed to him personally?
52.mohsin_khan: Nay, everyone of them desires that he should be given pages spread out (coming from Allah with a writing that Islam is the right religion, and Muhammad SAW has come with the truth from Allah the Lord of the heavens and earth, etc.).
52.arberry: Nay, every man of them desires to be -- given -- scrolls unrolled.

53.sahih_international: No! But they do not fear the Hereafter.
53.pickthall: Nay, verily. They fear not the Hereafter.
53.yusuf_ali: By no means! But they fear not the Hereafter,
53.shakir: Nay! but they do not fear the hereafter.
53.muhammad_sarwar: This will certainly never be the case! In fact, they are not afraid of the Day of Judgment.
53.mohsin_khan: Nay! But they fear not the Hereafter (from Allah's punishment).
53.arberry: No indeed; but they do not fear the Hereafter.

54.sahih_international: No! Indeed, the Qur'an is a reminder
54.pickthall: Nay, verily. Lo! this is an Admonishment.
54.yusuf_ali: Nay, this surely is an admonition:
54.shakir: Nay! it is surely an admonition.
54.muhammad_sarwar: There is no doubt that the Quran is a guide.
54.mohsin_khan: Nay, verily, this (Quran) is an admonition,
54.arberry: No indeed; surely it is a Reminder;

55.sahih_international: Then whoever wills will remember it.
55.yusuf_ali: Let any who will, keep it in remembrance!
55.shakir: So whoever pleases may mind it.
55.muhammad_sarwar: Let anyone who seeks guidance do so.
55.mohsin_khan: So whosoever will (let him read it), and receive admonition (from it)!
55.arberry: so whoever wills shall remember it.

56.sahih_international: And they will not remember except that Allah wills. He is worthy of fear and adequate for [granting] forgiveness.
56.pickthall: And they will not heed unless Allah willeth (it). He is the fount of fear. He is the fount of Mercy.
56.yusuf_ali: But none will keep it in remembrance except as Allah wills: He is the Lord of Righteousness, and the Lord of Forgiveness.
56.shakir: And they will not mind unless Allah please. He is worthy to be feared and worthy to forgive.
56.muhammad_sarwar: No one will seek guidance unless God wills it. He alone is worthy of being feared and He is the Source of Forgiveness.
56.mohsin_khan: And they will not receive admonition unless Allah wills; He (Allah) is the One, deserving that mankind should be afraid of, and should be dutiful to Him, and should not take any Ilah (God) along with Him, and He is the One Who forgives (sins).
56.arberry: And they will not remember, except that God wills; He is worthy to be feared, -- worthy to forgive.
